content:
Just looking at some of the comments here will reveal a group of people who vocally oppose all AI tools, including Apple Intelligence. This group may be a minority, but their voices are particularly loud. This situation has given rise to an unofficial tool that lets users disable this feature on Mac and delete all downloaded Siri AI models.

We mentioned yesterday that doing so may come with risks, but some now suggest that Apple, to protect hardware sales, may ultimately have to officially support the ability to remove AI...

In recent years, opposition to generative AI has continued to grow in society, with opponents citing a wide range of reasons — from concerns about the survival of the human species to simply not wanting their devices occupied by unnecessary AI storage space.

The latest Apple Intelligence models require up to 14GB of storage space, which has a considerable impact on 256GB models, if you don't want these features. This is why independent developer Om Lahore has developed a tool called RemoveMacAI.

Posted by GoldGrapes

"Minority but loud" aside, you're also saying their behaviour threatens hardware sales, so Apple must support an OS-level AI removal feature? How could a minority group possibly affect sales figures?

We reminded yesterday that using this tool is not without risks. Since Apple Intelligence is now deeply embedded in macOS 27, it may cause unexpected impacts on some basic functions.

However, some believe Apple may eventually have to provide an official way to remove Apple Intelligence on Mac. John Gruber of Daring Fireball specifically noted that some organisations have already banned the installation of AI tools.

To be clear, Apple already provides quite a few management options for organisations using device management. Apple says organisations can "restrict the use" of certain Apple Intelligence features, and there are independent toggles to turn individual features on or off one by one. What's currently missing is a master switch to disable all Apple Intelligence features at once, along with an option to remove downloaded models altogether.

This issue is not yet an urgent one, but as future Macs begin to drop support for older versions of macOS, if it remains impossible to easily remove AI models, it could very well start affecting Apple's hardware sales.
